source.title: Irish News and Belfast Morning News, 30 May 1908, p. 8 ("Armagh Rural Council"); nominations from the Armagh Guardian, 1 May 1908, p. 3 ("For Armagh Rural Council": nominations; "a" = against direct labour, "d l" = direct labour)
source.publisher: Irish News and Belfast Morning News (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: every figure read from the page image

note: Triennial election of the rural district council, polled 27 May 1908; "there were only six contests". Ballyards (Andrew Davidson, George Brown, Thomas Quinn, senr., nominated) is not in the results; the Irish News says the Nationalists gained a seat there, but the members returned were not found, so it is not filed. The nomination list marks candidates "a" (against direct labour) or "d l" (direct labour); these are not party labels and are not filed as such. Polled 27 May 1908. "As in the County Council elections, the question of direct labour as against the contract system in road maintenance entered largely into the contests." The nomination list prints "Hugh W Geary". "The Nationalists have gained two seats, viz., in the divisions of Clady and Ballyards."
